chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Aziz Al-Abdi, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who fractured a bone of a slave, he (peace be upon him) said: Upon him is half of the tenth of his price.

key_terms.شَجَّ: to fracture or break a bone

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for fracturing a slave's bone in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of Ubayd ibn Zurara to Imam al-Sadiq (AS), clarifies the specific calculation of *diyah* (blood money) for fracturing a prominent bone (*mudhihah*) in a slave. It establishes a precise financial liability of half of one-tenth (5%) of the slave's market value, reflecting the nuanced application of Islamic jurisprudence to property rights and bodily injury in the pre-modern economic context.
